stories.title: Decron Properties Buys 163-Unit Property in L.A.’s Miracle Mile for $114M
stories.excerpt: Decron Properties has acquired a 163-unit property in Los Angeles’ Miracle Mile for $114 million as the firm’s first L.A. deal in nearly two years. The Los Angeles-based investment firm acquired the asset at 5550 Wilshire Boulevard, a residential and retail property developed in 2010, at what Decron described as a substantial discount to replacement cost. After focusing on Sun Belt markets, the firm said it continues to pursue opportunities across Los Angeles, San Jose, Orange County, San Diego and Seattle as well. “Our growth-market strategy has never been a referendum on Los Angeles,” Decron President and CEO David Nagel said in a statement. “For a period, the risk-adjusted returns here simply weren’t competitive with what we were finding in the Sun Belt markets.” Nagel added that Los Angeles remains “one of the nation’s most important and chronically undersupplied housing markets,” where new supply is difficult and expensive to build. 5550 Wilshire includes one-, two- and three-bedroom apartments and townhomes. Amenities include a pool and spa, a resident lounge, a private movie theater and rooftop lounges. The property also includes 14,686 square feet of ground-floor retail that is fully leased to tenants that include Chipotle, Five Guys and FedEx Office. JLL’s Blake Rogers represented both Decron and the seller in the transaction. Decron owns and manages nearly 10,000 multifamily units and about 1 million square feet of retail across California, Washington and Arizona, with a portfolio totaling roughly 8.7 million square feet. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Decron Properties acquired 163-unit Miracle Mile property for $114M, first L.A. deal in 2 years.
Buyer cited 'substantial discount to replacement cost' in chronically undersupplied L.A. housing market.
Firm pivoting from Sun Belt focus; signals L.A. risk-adjusted returns now competitive.
stories.summary: Decron Properties paid $114 million for a 2010-built, 163-unit residential property at 5550 Wilshire Boulevard in Los Angeles' Miracle Mile, marking the firm's return to the L.A. market after a two-year absence focused on Sun Belt growth. The deal was struck at a substantial discount to replacement cost, according to the buyer. The acquisition signals a strategic pivot: after finding superior risk-adjusted returns in the Sun Belt, the developer now sees L.A.'s chronic undersupply and high construction barriers as creating value opportunities again.
stories.impact: Decron's re-entry into L.A. on a value basis suggests cap-rate compression in Sun Belt markets has narrowed the spread; L.A.'s entitlement and construction-cost barriers are creating a moat that makes legacy built assets attractive relative to new development. Watch for more institutional capital returning to L.A. if replacement-cost discounts persist—signals softening development feasibility in the Sun Belt.

stories.title: Corebridge Financial Refis Meatpacking Office Property With $293M Loan
stories.excerpt: A joint venture between Aurora Capital Associates and William Gottlieb Real Estate has sealed a $293 million loan to refinance a mixed-use asset in Manhattan’s Meatpacking District, according to a release. Corebridge Financial provided the fixed-rate, permanent loan on the 158,957-square-foot building at 40 10th Avenue. The 2019-built property features 112,241 square feet of office space and 46,176 square feet of retail on the first two floors. Walker & Dunlop negotiated the debt with a team consisting of Dustin Stolly, Aaron Appel, Jonathan Schwartz, Keith Kurland, Adam Schwartz, Sean Reimer, Jordan Casella and Stanley Cayre. “40 10th Avenue stands out in building quality, location and experience — all elements that differentiate a property for tenants,” Stolly, senior managing director of the capital markets institutional advisory team at Walker & Dunlop, said in a statement. “The fully leased office component, institutional tenant roster and substantial outdoor space demonstrate the continued demand for high-touch, well-located workplaces in New York.” The 10-story building has office tenants that include Starwood Capital Group, WestCap Management, RTW Investments, Stripes and Checkout.com. The retail portion of the property is occupied by Hyundai Motor. The property is positioned for success, according to Walker & Dunlop, since the Meatpacking District is one of Manhattan’s most supply-constrained office and retail submarkets. Aurora Capital Associates and William Gottlieb Real Estate landed a $150 million loan from Deutsche Pfandbriefbank in June 2020 to refinance construction debt to build the property, CO first reported at the time. Corebridge Financial, Aurora Capital and William Gottlieb Real Estate did not immediately return requests for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Aurora Capital and Gottlieb RE refinanced Manhattan Meatpacking mixed-use asset for $293M permanent loan.
Property fully leased office, 112K SF, built 2019; Corebridge provided fixed-rate permanent debt.
Lender emphasized 'continued demand for high-touch, well-located workplaces' in NYC.
stories.summary: A joint venture between Aurora Capital Associates and William Gottlieb Real Estate closed a $293 million permanent, fixed-rate refinance from Corebridge Financial on 40 10th Avenue, a 2019-built, 158,957-square-foot mixed-use asset in Manhattan's Meatpacking District. The property comprises 112,241 SF of fully leased office and 46,176 SF of ground-floor retail. The lender's framing emphasized institutional tenant quality and strong demand for premium-located workspace.
stories.impact: Full occupancy and a fixed-rate permanent refinance on a high-quality Manhattan office asset suggest institutional lenders are still willing to finance best-in-class office in prime submarkets, but selectivity remains acute. This refi (likely at lower rates than construction-period floating debt) does not signal broad office market recovery—it reflects the bifurcation favoring trophy assets in Manhattan's densest neighborhoods over secondary/tertiary office.

stories.title: Affinius Capital Originates $130M Construction Loan for Chicago MF Development
stories.excerpt: Affinius Capital has originated a $130.4 million construction loan to finance 1000 W. Jackson, a multifamily development located in Chicago’s West Loop submarket. The 25-story development will feature 380 units and more than 21,500 square feet of ground-floor commercial space, pre-leased to ALDI, Inc. The loan was made to a joint venture between Mavrek Development, a Chicago-based developer, and Fengate Asset Management. The financing was arranged by John Parrett of CBRE. Upon completion, 1000 W. Jackson will deliver 380 units, ranging from studios to three-bedroom units. The development will offer approximately 31,000 square feet of indoor and outdoor amenities. Strategically located at the corner of West Jackson Boulevard and South Morgan Street, the property sits within Chicago’s West Loop, three blocks south of Fulton Market, with walkable access to major employment centers, transit, and neighborhood amenities. The project will be constructed by Skender, with Eckenhoff Saunders serving as architect. The conversations behind tomorrow’s apartment deals happen at Connect Apartments on September 22 in LA. Connect with the capital sources, owners, developers, and brokers driving multifamily investment. Learn more and reserve your seat at www.connectapts2026.com. bullets: Affinius Capital originated $130.4M construction loan for 380-unit Chicago West Loop multifamily development.
1000 W. Jackson: 25-story, ground-floor anchored by ALDI pre-lease, built by Skender.
Joint venture: Mavrek Development and Fengate Asset Management; near Fulton Market submarket.
stories.summary: Affinius Capital provided a $130.4 million construction loan to a joint venture of Mavrek Development and Fengate Asset Management for 1000 W. Jackson, a 380-unit, 25-story multifamily development in Chicago's West Loop. The project includes over 21,500 square feet of ground-floor commercial space pre-leased to ALDI, Inc., plus 31,000 SF of indoor/outdoor amenities. Located three blocks south of Fulton Market near major transit and employment, the project is being constructed by Skender.
stories.impact: Robust construction financing on a large, transit-oriented, grocery-anchored mixed-use project in West Loop signals strong lender confidence in Chicago's walkable urban submarket demand. ALDI pre-lease de-risks ground-floor economics and anchors foot traffic; this type of deal suggests Chicago dev community is capturing renewed downtown/urban residential demand. Watch for similar urban-infill construction deals in Chicago; the market is likely seeing sustained migration into the Loop and surrounding neighborhoods.

stories.title: U.S. Office Sector Faces $289B of Loan Maturities
stories.excerpt: Risk and uncertainty in the U.S. office sector look poised to grow due to increasingly volatile economic conditions compounding the challenges stemming from office loan maturities, which are expected to peak throughout the next few years. Yardi Matrix research data show that 14,000 office properties are encumbered by loans that have recently matured or are due to mature by the end of 2028 with loans totaling $289.2 billion, or 33.5% of total loan volume. “Nearly 59% of these loans originated before 2021 with the baked-in assumption that high demand would sustain loan obligations through maturity,” according to a report from Yardi Systems’ CommercialCafe. “However, with office-using jobs declining since mid-2023, existing demand being concentrated largely in the highest quality assets and hybrid work putting down persistent roots (among other factors), pressure is building as office loans approach maturity.” Peter Kolaczynski, director, Yardi Research, said, “The office debt problem is not going away yet. With interest rates and stubbornly low physical occupancy both adding to the headwind, the expectation is for increased delinquencies and distress.” The post U.S. Office Sector Faces $289B of Loan Maturities appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: 14,000 U.S. office properties face $289.2B loan maturities through end of 2028; 33.5% of total office debt.
59% of loans originated pre-2021 with high-demand assumptions; office jobs declining since mid-2023.
Rising delinquencies and distress expected; interest rates and low occupancy compound headwinds.
stories.summary: Yardi Matrix research identified 14,000 office properties encumbered by $289.2 billion in loans maturing by end of 2028, representing 33.5% of total office loan volume. Nearly 59% of these loans were originated before 2021 under assumptions of sustained high demand; however, office-using employment has declined since mid-2023, hybrid work persists, and demand is concentrated in highest-quality assets. Analysts expect increased delinquencies and distress as loans mature into a weaker refinancing environment.
stories.impact: The office maturity wall creates a long-tail distress pipeline that will suppress returns on stabilized office assets and refinancings through 2028+, but also creates opportunity windows for selective, well-capitalized buyers to acquire trophy office at discounts. More critically for multifamily developers: office distress and credit stress will dampen cross-collateralized CMBS deals and reduce lender appetite for speculative development. Capital that might chase development will instead chase office value-add. Expect sustained tight construction financing in 2025–2026.

stories.title: Endura Starts Work on 324-Unit Boerne Apartment Community
stories.excerpt: Endura Advisory Group broke ground on The Oaks of Cibolo Creek, a 324 unit apartment complex in Boerne, Texas. The project will sit on 20 acres about 2.5 miles from the downtown area. Designed by Dallas-based UD Architects, with Franklin Construction, Ltd. as the contractor, the property will feature units averaging 918 square feet, with select homes offering private yards. The property will be managed by Greystar, with financing provided through a HUD 221(d)(4) loan secured through the Mason Joseph Company. Residents will enjoy a comprehensive suite of outdoor and community amenities. These amenities include a state-of-the-art clubhouse with a serving area, a resort-style swimming pool featuring a sun deck, a modern fitness center, a dog park and washing station, a pickleball court, and secured access entry. The post Endura Starts Work on 324-Unit Boerne Apartment Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Endura Advisory Group broke ground on 324-unit apartment community in Boerne, Texas (near San Antonio).
The Oaks of Cibolo Creek: 20-acre site, 2.5 miles from downtown; HUD 221(d)(4) financing.
Units avg. 918 SF; managed by Greystar; full amenity suite including pool, fitness, pickleball.
stories.summary: Endura Advisory Group started construction on The Oaks of Cibolo Creek, a 324-unit apartment community in Boerne, Texas, a suburban/exurban community near San Antonio. Sitting on 20 acres about 2.5 miles from downtown, the project is financed via a HUD 221(d)(4) loan (affordable/workforce housing-eligible) and will be managed by Greystar. Units average 918 square feet and the property includes a comprehensive amenity package with pools, fitness, dog park, and pickleball.
stories.impact: HUD 221(d)(4) financing on a suburban Texas development signals sustained demand for affordable/workforce housing in growth corridors outside major metros. Boerne's proximity to San Antonio (growing tech/manufacturing hub) and the Hill Country's demographic appeal support this. The deal suggests capital is flowing toward workforce housing and suburban infill in high-migration regions where rent growth and demographic tailwinds are strong but construction costs remain manageable outside urban cores.

stories.title: Work Underway on New $116M Sedona Resort
stories.excerpt: R.D. Olson Construction has broken ground on the $116 million, 70-key Senoa Resort & Spa on 11.5 acres in Sedona, Arizona, with an opening slated for late 2028. The villa-style wellness resort will be located at 150 Schnebly Hill Road in Sedona. The site is minutes from downtown Sedona. R.D. Olson Construction is working with R.D. Olson Development and Senoa Investment Partners on the project. AO is the architect of record, and WATG is the entitlement architect. The resort will comprise 29 free-standing structures. Planned amenities include a two-story creekside restaurant, a Red Rock Saloon bar concept, an event lawn with green foliage and private creek access, and a poolside area. The resort will also include a 5,500-square-foot spa and a 3,200-square-foot multipurpose space for meetings and events. Guest accommodations are planned to range from 600-square-foot king bedrooms to 720-square-foot suites and a 1,300-square-foot presidential suite. The rooms are planned with indoor-outdoor layouts. bullets: R.D. Olson Construction broke ground on $116M, 70-key Senoa Resort & Spa in Sedona, Arizona.
Villa-style wellness resort; 11.5 acres at 150 Schnebly Hill Road; opening late 2028.
29 freestanding structures; 5,500 SF spa, 2-story restaurant, creek access; rooms 600–1,300 SF.
stories.summary: R.D. Olson Construction has begun work on the Senoa Resort & Spa, a $116 million, 70-key villa-style wellness resort on 11.5 acres in Sedona, Arizona, with an expected opening in late 2028. The property comprises 29 freestanding guest structures ranging from 600 to 1,300 square feet, along with a 5,500-square-foot spa, creekside restaurant, bar, event lawn, and multipurpose meeting space.
stories.impact: Not directly relevant to multifamily development. This is a hospitality/resort development in a destination market; no bearing on apartment demand, supply, financing, or costs in the multifamily sector.

stories.title: Sares Regis Trades Henderson Rental Asset for $41M
stories.excerpt: Authentic Capital Group acquired Miro at the Parc, a 164-unit multifamily community located at 1651 American Pacific Dr in Henderson, NV, in a $41 million transaction. Newmark’s Jonathan Merhaut and Curt Allsop arranged the sale on behalf of seller, Sares Regis Multifamily Investment Management. Newmark’s Lee Redmond and Alec Newman arranged the $24.75 million financing on behalf of Authentic Capital Group. Located in the Henderson submarket of Las Vegas, Miro at the Parc benefits from an A+ submarket location, proximity to major employment centers and large floorplans. The community is situated within Green Valley, one of Las Vegas’ most established residential corridors, where sustained population growth and limited housing inventory continue to support multifamily demand. Southern Nevada continues to attract institutional and private capital as investors seek exposure to markets characterized by favorable migration patterns, economic diversification and strong multifamily fundamentals, according to Newmark Research. The post Sares Regis Trades Henderson Rental Asset for $41M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Authentic Capital Group acquired 164-unit Miro at the Parc in Henderson, Nevada for $41M.
Seller: Sares Regis Multifamily Investment Management; buyer financed $24.75M via Newmark.
Green Valley submarket (Las Vegas); sustained population growth, limited inventory supporting demand.
stories.summary: Authentic Capital Group purchased Miro at the Parc, a 164-unit multifamily community in Henderson's Green Valley submarket (Las Vegas metro), for $41 million. Sares Regis Multifamily Investment Management was the seller. Newmark arranged $24.75 million in financing for the buyer. The property is positioned in one of Las Vegas' most established residential corridors, benefiting from sustained population growth and limited housing inventory.
stories.impact: Sares Regis' exit from this core stabilized asset signals either portfolio optimization (raising capital for higher-return development) or a rotation away from the market. Authentic Capital's entry at a $250K/unit basis in a tight supply market (Green Valley) suggests institutional capital continues to view Las Vegas Sun Belt fundamentals as solid despite broader Sunbelt cap-rate compression. Watch for increased trading activity in Las Vegas core assets as sponsors recycle capital; limited inventory in Green Valley will support rent growth regardless.

stories.title: Stroller Brand Uppababy Relocates Store to 156 Montague Street in Brooklyn Heights
stories.excerpt: Known for its distinctive strollers, baby gear brand Uppababy is relocating its store within Brooklyn, Commercial Observer has learned. The high-end baby accessories brand is opening a 3,780-square-foot brick-and-mortar location at Owen Realty’s 156 Montague Street in Brooklyn Heights, according to broker JLL. Uppababy will move next year from 90 Smith Street in Cobble Hill, where it established its Brooklyn retail and service “hub” in about 2019. JLL did not immediately provide the length of the lease or the asking rent for the space, but the average retail asking rent along nearby Fulton Street was $190 per square foot in 2025, according to the most recent retail report from the Real Estate Board of New York. “Brooklyn is an important market for Uppababy, and this relocation allows us to build on the relationships we have developed with local families,” Bob Monahan, co-founder and CEO of Uppababy, said in a statement. “Brooklyn Heights has a strong community of young and growing families, and the Montague Street location gives us the space and accessibility to deliver the hands-on product experience and personalized service that define our hub stores.” Uppababy manufactures and sells strollers, car seats, highchairs and other products for infants. Its top-of-the-line Vista V3 stroller, described on the company’s website as a “best seller,” retails for $1,000. JLL’s Jesse Wolff and Elijah Mehl represented the tenant in the transaction while Ryan Condren and George Danut, also from JLL, negotiated on behalf of Owen Realty. Owen Realty, which uses the LLC Montague Realty Development Associates, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. “Montague Street offers the neighborhood density, visibility and accessibility that work well for family focused retailers like Uppababy,” Wolff said in a statement. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Uppababy (baby gear brand) relocating Brooklyn flagship to 156 Montague Street, Brooklyn Heights.
3,780 SF retail lease; moving from Cobble Hill (90 Smith St) after ~6 years; opens next year.
Brooklyn Heights cited for young, growing family demographic; avg. nearby retail asking rent ~$190/SF.
stories.summary: High-end baby accessories brand Uppababy is relocating its Brooklyn retail and service hub to a 3,780-square-foot space at 156 Montague Street in Brooklyn Heights, leaving its Cobble Hill location (90 Smith Street) after approximately six years. The company cited Brooklyn Heights' strong community of young and growing families as key to the move. Average retail asking rents along nearby Fulton Street are approximately $190 per square foot.
stories.impact: Uppababy's relocation to Brooklyn Heights signals retailer confidence in the neighborhood's demographic profile (young families, high purchasing power) and its retail resilience post-pandemic. Brooklyn Heights' strong family-oriented positioning supports ground-floor retail demand in new/renovated apartment buildings; developers should prioritize family-centric retail tenants (pediatrics, children's education, wellness, dining) in Brooklyn multifamily projects targeting young households with children.

stories.title: Institutional and Private Equity Investors: Their Commercial Real Estate Hot Takes
stories.excerpt: Commercial Observer’s annual Institutional Investor & Private Equity Forum took center stage at 237 Park Avenue in Midtown Manhattan on Sept. 16, when some of the biggest names in commercial real estate investment offered their thoughts on the state of capital markets. Under the shadow of the Federal Reserve set to raise short-term interest rates for the first time in three years (which they did that very afternoon), Blackstone’s Katie Keenan, global head of core-plus real estate and CEO of Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust (BREIT), sat down with Jennifer Recine, partner at King & Spalding, to host the opening keynote. Keenan enumerated reasons why the U.S. market is currently experiencing “a compelling backdrop for real estate” largely from an ongoing reset in asset values, a growth in cash flows, and the supply in asset classes such as multifamily and retail at the lowest levels in decades. She also touched on the accelerating demand from artificial intelligence, digitalization, and e-commerce. “When you have growing demand and flat, or down, supply, it’s a meaningful impact on what you see from a cash flow and growth perspective,” Keenan said. “The debt capital markets … are as healthy as I’ve seen them in a long time. Capital is readily available and it’s well priced.” Keenan noted that 90 percent of Blackstone’s core-plus portfolio consists of logistics, data centers and multifamily, and that these assets benefit from the conservative approach that core-plus investing uniquely prioritizes. bullets: Blackstone BREIT CEO highlighted multifamily and retail supply at 'lowest levels in decades.'
Fed raised rates for first time in 3 years (Sept. 2024); Blackstone notes 'compelling backdrop' for real estate.
Growing demand from AI, digitalization, e-commerce; reset in asset values creating opportunity.
stories.summary: At Commercial Observer's Institutional Investor & Private Equity Forum on September 16, Blackstone's Katie Keenan, global head of core-plus real estate and CEO of BREIT, characterized the U.S. real estate market as experiencing 'a compelling backdrop' driven by asset value resets, growing cash flows, and notably low supply in multifamily and retail sectors—at decade-low levels. She also cited accelerating demand from AI, digitalization, and e-commerce as growth vectors. This commentary occurred as the Federal Reserve announced its first rate increase in three years.
stories.impact: Blackstone's explicit emphasis on multifamily supply scarcity and demand growth signals institutional capital is confident in the asset class fundamentals and likely to pursue development-stage deals and acquisitions. The Fed's rate pivot (pause/hike cycle ending) may extend the window for favorable construction financing into 2025. Expect institutional capital (pension funds, insurance, BREIT) to compete aggressively for multifamily land, development-stage assets, and JV equity in growth markets.

stories.title: A Different Downtown San Diego Is Taking Shape
stories.excerpt: Downtown San Diego looks a lot different than it did a year ago. People who haven’t spent much time there recently may still picture the challenges that dominated conversations before: quiet streets, empty storefronts, concerns about safety, and office towers that have too much vacant space. Some of those challenges remain. Office vacancy is still a real issue with recent estimates in the 20 percent range as employers rethink their space needs amid hybrid work models. But some things have changed. Downtown increasingly feels like it has reached a turning point. The question isn’t whether it will recover, but how it will recover, and what progress is already underway. One reason for the improvement is that momentum isn’t coming from a single source. Businesses, residents, visitors, universities, cultural institutions, philanthropy and new investment are all contributing to the area’s revival. The Downtown San Diego Partnership, for example, has made cleaner, safer and more welcoming streets a priority. The Clean & Safe team serves six Downtown neighborhoods over 1.15 square miles, 280 blocks and more than 13,000 unique parcels within the Property and Business Improvement District. Organizations like the Prebys Foundation are also making significant investments in downtown real estate and public life. Prebys recently acquired the long-vacant California Theater site for $6.3 million, purchased major office properties including Wells Fargo Plaza and a Little Italy headquarters, and partnered on a grand Civic Center redesign. Its investment in the historic 24-story 401 B Street tower, for example, is particularly telling. The foundation described the acquisition as “a declaration of belief in what downtown can become: a vibrant hub of commerce, culture and civic life that welcomes all who call this region home and all who are drawn to its promise.” Educational and cultural institutions are adding another layer of activity. bullets: Downtown San Diego office vacancy ~20% amid hybrid work; but broader recovery momentum is diversifying.
Revival driven by multiple sources: businesses, residents, universities, cultural orgs, philanthropy, new investment.
Clean & Safe and Downtown San Diego Partnership initiatives improving streetscape and perceived safety.
stories.summary: Downtown San Diego is undergoing a recovery inflection, moving beyond questions of 'if' to 'how' and 'what.' While office vacancy remains elevated at approximately 20% due to hybrid work, the recovery is being catalyzed by multiple actors—businesses, residents, universities, cultural institutions, philanthropic organizations, and new capital—rather than a single source. The Downtown San Diego Partnership and its Clean & Safe team have made visible improvements to streetscape quality and public safety.
stories.impact: Downtown San Diego's diversified recovery (not office-dependent) suggests mixed-use, residential-focused development and adaptive reuse projects are finding tailwinds. The presence of universities, cultural anchors, and improving public realm creates conditions for residential infill and young-professional housing to absorb space. Developers should assess entry opportunities in downtown residential and live-work conversion projects; office vacancy creates zoning/entitlement leverage, but true demand is coming from residents and institutional anchors, not office tenants.
